passages.text: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah became king when he was twenty-one years old.
He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years.
His mother was Hamutal.
Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah.
She came from Libnah.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חֲמִיטַל בַּֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה׃

passages.text: And Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was king in Jerusalem.
Zedekiah did evil things.
The LORD saw Zedekiah’s evil.
Jehoiakim was a king before Zedekiah.
Jehoiakim also did evil things.
Zedekiah did evil just like Jehoiakim.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוֹיָקִֽים׃

passages.text: For because of the anger of the LORD, all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until He finally banished them from His presence. And Zedekiah also rebelled against the king of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The LORD became angry with Jerusalem and Judah.
His anger caused all these things to happen there.
He finally banished the people from His presence.
Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ עַל־ אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה עַד־ הִשְׁלִיכ֥וֹ אוֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his entire army. They encamped outside the city and built a siege wall all around it.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was king in Jerusalem.
Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, something happened.
On the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem.
He brought his entire army with him.
They marched against Jerusalem.
They set up camp outside the city.
They built a siege wall all around Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ בַשָּׁנָ֨ה הַתְּשִׁעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒ בָּ֠א נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֜ל ה֤וּא וְכָל־ חֵילוֹ֙ עַל־ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּבְנ֥וּ עָלֶ֛יהָ דָּיֵ֖ק סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: And the city was kept under siege until King Zedekiah’s eleventh year.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is the city.
Babylon’s army surrounded Jerusalem.
They kept the city under siege.
This siege lasted a long time.
The siege continued until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah’s reign.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֥א הָעִ֖יר בַּמָּצ֑וֹר עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was so severe that the people of the land had no food.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem lived in the city.
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He and his army surrounded Jerusalem.
They built a siege wall around the city.
They kept the city under siege for a long time.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, a famine struck the city.
The famine became very severe.
The people of the land had no food.
passages.original: בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בָּעִ֑יר וְלֹא־ הָיָ֥ה לֶ֖חֶם לְעַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Then the city was breached; and though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, all the men of war fled the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They headed toward the Arabah, but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was separated from him.
passages.sermon:
The Babylonian army, also called the Chaldeans, surrounded Jerusalem.
The city wall was broken through.
All the soldiers in Jerusalem tried to escape.
They left the city at night.
They went out through a gate between two walls.
This gate was near the king’s garden.
The soldiers headed toward the Arabah.
The Chaldean army chased after King Zedekiah.
They caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.
All of Zedekiah’s soldiers scattered and left him.
passages.original: וַתִּבָּקַ֣ע הָעִ֗יר וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֡ה יִבְרְחוּ֩ וַיֵּצְא֨וּ מֵהָעִ֜יר לַ֗יְלָה דֶּ֜רֶךְ שַׁ֤עַר בֵּין־ הַחֹמֹתַ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ גַּ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכַשְׂדִּ֥ים עַל־ הָעִ֖יר סָבִ֑יב וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָעֲרָבָֽה׃ וַיִּרְדְּפ֤וּ חֵיל־ כַּשְׂדִּים֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּשִּׂ֥יגוּ אֶת־ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת יְרֵח֑וֹ וְכָל־ חֵיל֔וֹ נָפֹ֖צוּ מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: The Chaldeans seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on Zedekiah.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans captured King Zedekiah.
They took Zedekiah to the king of Babylon.
The king of Babylon was at Riblah.
Riblah is in the land of Hamath.
The king of Babylon spoke judgment to Zedekiah.
passages.original: וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּעֲל֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל־ מֶ֧לֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל רִבְלָ֖תָה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁפָּטִֽים׃

passages.text: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also killed all the officials of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon was a powerful foreign ruler.
He captured Zedekiah, the king of Judah.
They were at Riblah, a city in the land of Hamath.
The king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah.
He did this while Zedekiah was watching.
The king of Babylon also killed all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁחַ֧ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ לְעֵינָ֑יו וְגַ֛ם אֶת־ כָּל־ שָׂרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה שָׁחַ֥ט בְּרִבְלָֽתָה׃

passages.text: Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon, where he kept him in custody until his dying day.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon captured Zedekiah.
The king of Babylon blinded Zedekiah.
He put bronze shackles on Zedekiah.
He took Zedekiah to Babylon.
He kept Zedekiah in prison until Zedekiah died.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ עֵינֵ֥י צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ עִוֵּ֑ר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בַֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֗יִם וַיְבִאֵ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ בָּבֶ֔לָה וַיִּתְּנֵ֥הוּ בְבֵית הַפְּקֻדֹּ֖ת עַד־ י֥וֹם מוֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign over Babylon, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He ruled for nineteen years.
The fifth month came.
It was the tenth day of that month.
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
He served the king of Babylon.
Nebuzaradan entered Jerusalem.
passages.original: וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ הִ֗יא שְׁנַת֙ תְּשַֽׁע־ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֑ל בָּ֗א נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב־ טַבָּחִ֔ים עָמַ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem—every significant building.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
He served the king of Babylon.
Nebuzaradan entered Jerusalem.
He set fire to the house of the LORD.
He burned the royal palace.
He burned all the houses in Jerusalem.
He destroyed every important building with fire.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת־ בֵּית־ יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ בָּתֵּ֧י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְאֶת־ כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית הַגָּד֖וֹל שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: And the whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans were a powerful army from Babylon.
Nebuzaradan was their captain of the guard.
The Chaldean army obeyed Nebuzaradan.
They broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.
They destroyed every wall that protected the city.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ כָּל־ חֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל־ חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶת־ רַב־ טַבָּחִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people and those who remained in the city, along with the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon and the rest of the craftsmen.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for the king of Babylon.
He took some of the poorest people from Jerusalem.
He also took the people who still remained in the city.
He took the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon.
He took the rest of the craftsmen.
Nebuzaradan carried all these people into exile.
passages.original: וּמִדַּלּ֨וֹת הָעָ֜ם וְֽאֶת־ יֶ֥תֶר הָעָ֣ם׀ הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר וְאֶת־ הַנֹּֽפְלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽפְלוּ֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת יֶ֣תֶר הָֽאָמ֑וֹן הֶגְלָ֕ה נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־ טַבָּחִֽים׃

passages.text: But Nebuzaradan captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for the Chaldeans.
He left behind some of the poorest people in the land.
He allowed these poor people to remain.
He gave them the work of tending vineyards.
He also gave them the work of farming the fields.
passages.original: וּמִדַּלּ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֕יר נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֑ים לְכֹרְמִ֖ים וּלְיֹגְבִֽים׃

passages.text: Moreover, the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars and stands and the bronze Sea in the house of the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans entered the house of the LORD.
They found the bronze pillars there.
They found the bronze stands there.
They found the bronze Sea there.
The Chaldeans broke the bronze pillars.
They broke the bronze stands.
They broke the bronze Sea.
They took all the bronze from these objects.
They carried all the bronze to Babylon.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְבֵית־ יְהוָ֗ה וְֽאֶת־ הַמְּכֹנ֞וֹת וְאֶת־ יָ֧ם הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבֵית־ יְהוָ֖ה שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־ כָּל־ נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the articles of bronze used in the temple service.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans entered the house of the LORD.
They took many items from the temple.
They took the bronze pots.
They took the bronze shovels.
They took the bronze wick trimmers.
They took the bronze sprinkling bowls.
They took the bronze dishes.
They took all the bronze articles used for temple service.
They carried all these bronze items away.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַ֠סִּרוֹת וְאֶת־ הַיָּעִ֨ים וְאֶת־ הַֽמְזַמְּר֜וֹת וְאֶת־ הַמִּזְרָקֹ֣ת וְאֶת־ הַכַּפּ֗וֹת וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ כְּלֵ֧י הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר־ יְשָׁרְת֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם לָקָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: The captain of the guard also took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and drink offering bowls—anything made of pure gold or fine silver.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the guard took many items from the temple.
He took the basins.
He took the censers.
He took the sprinkling bowls.
He took the pots.
He took the lampstands.
He took the pans.
He took the drink offering bowls.
He took every item made of pure gold.
He took every item made of fine silver.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַ֠סִּפִּים וְאֶת־ הַמַּחְתּ֨וֹת וְאֶת־ הַמִּזְרָק֜וֹת וְאֶת־ הַסִּיר֣וֹת וְאֶת־ הַמְּנֹר֗וֹת וְאֶת־ הַכַּפּוֹת֙ וְאֶת־ הַמְּנַקִי֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר זָהָב֙ זָהָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁר־ כֶּ֖סֶף כָּ֑סֶף לָקַ֖ח רַב־ טַבָּחִֽים׃

passages.text: As for the two pillars, the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands that King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the weight of the bronze from all these articles was beyond measure.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made many large bronze items for the house of the LORD.
He made two pillars.
He made one large basin called the Sea.
He made twelve bronze bulls to go under the Sea.
He made movable stands.
All these items were made of bronze.
No one could measure the total weight of the bronze used for these items.
passages.original: הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים׀ שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם אֶחָד֙ וְהַבָּקָ֞ר שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֤ר נְחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁר־ תַּ֣חַת הַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־ הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם כָּל־ הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: Each pillar was eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference; each was hollow, four fingers thick.
passages.sermon:
Each pillar stood eighteen cubits tall.
Each pillar measured twelve cubits around.
Each pillar was hollow.
Each pillar had walls four fingers thick.
passages.original: וְהָעַמּוּדִ֗ים שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ קוֹמָה הָעַמֻּ֣ד הָאֶחָ֔ד וְח֛וּט שְׁתֵּים־ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה יְסֻבֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָבְי֛וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע אַצְבָּע֖וֹת נָבֽוּב׃

passages.text: The bronze capital atop one pillar was five cubits high, with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made two pillars for the house of the LORD.
Each pillar had a capital on top.
The capital was made of bronze.
The capital was five cubits high.
A network of bronze surrounded the capital.
Bronze pomegranates decorated the network around the capital.
The second pillar had a capital like the first.
The second pillar also had bronze pomegranates.
passages.original: וְכֹתֶ֨רֶת עָלָ֜יו נְחֹ֗שֶׁת וְקוֹמַ֨ת הַכֹּתֶ֥רֶת הָאַחַת֮ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּוֹת֒ וּשְׂבָכָ֨ה וְרִמּוֹנִ֧ים עַֽל־ הַכּוֹתֶ֛רֶת סָבִ֖יב הַכֹּ֣ל נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְכָאֵ֛לֶּה לַֽעַמּ֥וּד הַשֵּׁנִ֖י וְרִמּוֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: Each capital had ninety-six pomegranates on the sides, and a total of a hundred pomegranates were above the surrounding network.
passages.sermon:
Each capital had pomegranates on its sides.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides of each capital.
There were also pomegranates above the network that surrounded the capital.
The total number of pomegranates above the network was one hundred.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ הָֽרִמֹּנִ֔ים תִּשְׁעִ֥ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֖ה ר֑וּחָה כָּל־ הָרִמּוֹנִ֥ים מֵאָ֛ה עַל־ הַשְּׂבָכָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: The captain of the guard also took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the guard acted.
He took Seraiah.
Seraiah was the chief priest.
He took Zephaniah.
Zephaniah was the priest of second rank.
He took the three doorkeepers.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב־ טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת־ שְׂרָיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְאֶת־ צְפַנְיָ֖ה כֹּהֵ֣ן הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְאֶת־ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּֽף׃

passages.text: Of those still in the city, he took a court official who had been appointed over the men of war, as well as seven trusted royal advisers. He also took the scribe of the captain of the army, who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the city.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
He took people from the city.
He took one court official.
This official was in charge of the men of war.
He took seven men who advised the king.
These seven men were found in the city.
He took the scribe of the army’s captain.
This scribe had enlisted the people of the land.
He took sixty men from the people of the land.
These sixty men were found inside the city.
passages.original: וּמִן־ הָעִ֡יר לָקַח֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ הָיָ֥ה פָקִ֣יד׀ עַל־ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרֹאֵ֤י פְנֵי־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְא֣וּ בָעִ֔יר וְאֵ֗ת סֹפֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א הַמַּצְבִּ֖א אֶת־ עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מֵעַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
Nebuzaradan took these people.
He brought them to the king of Babylon.
He brought them to the king at Riblah.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אוֹתָ֔ם נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֑ים וַיֹּ֧לֶךְ אוֹתָ֛ם אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָֽתָה׃

passages.text: There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon was a powerful ruler.
He was in Riblah, a city in the land of Hamath.
He struck down the prisoners there.
He put them to death.
He took the people of Judah away from their land.
He sent Judah into exile.
passages.original: וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אוֹתָם֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֧ל וַיְמִתֵ֛ם בְּרִבְלָ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried away: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews; in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem; in Nebuchadnezzar’s twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried away 745 Jews. So in all, 4,600 people were taken away.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He took many people from Judah into exile.
In his seventh year, Nebuchadnezzar carried away 3,023 Jews.
In his eighteenth year, Nebuchadnezzar took 832 people from Jerusalem.
In his twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
Nebuzaradan carried away 745 Jews.
Altogether, 4,600 people were taken away.
passages.original: זֶ֣ה הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶגְלָ֖ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֑ר בִּשְׁנַת־ שֶׁ֕בַע יְהוּדִ֕ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃ בִּשְׁנַ֛ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֑ר מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם נֶ֕פֶשׁ שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם׃ בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שָׁלֹ֣שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים֮ לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֒ הֶגְלָ֗ה נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב־ טַבָּחִ֔ים יְהוּדִ֕ים נֶ֕פֶשׁ שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑ה כָּל־ נֶ֕פֶשׁ אַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiachin was the king of Judah.
The people of Babylon took him into exile.
He lived in exile for thirty-seven years.
Evil-merodach became king of Babylon.
It was the first year of Evil-merodach’s reign.
On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach acted.
Evil-merodach pardoned Jehoiachin.
Evil-merodach released Jehoiachin from prison.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּצֵ֥א אוֹת֖וֹ מִבֵּ֥ית הַכְּלִיא׃

passages.text: And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Evil-merodach was the king of Babylon.
Jehoiachin was the king of Judah.
Evil-merodach spoke kindly to Jehoiachin.
Evil-merodach set Jehoiachin’s throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ טֹב֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־ כִּסְא֔וֹ מִמַּ֗עַל לְכִסֵּ֧א מְלָכִים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiachin was the king of Judah.
The king of Babylon released Jehoiachin from prison.
Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes.
Jehoiachin ate bread at the king of Babylon’s table.
He ate there regularly.
He did this for the rest of his life.
passages.original: וְשִׁנָּ֕ה אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ וְאָכַ֨ל לֶ֧חֶם לְפָנָ֛יו תָּמִ֖יד כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו׃

passages.text: And the king of Babylon provided Jehoiachin a daily portion for the rest of his life, until the day of his death.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin food every day.
Jehoiachin received this food each day, without fail.
The king continued to provide for Jehoiachin until Jehoiachin died.
Jehoiachin had this daily portion for the rest of his life.
passages.original: וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַת֩ תָּמִ֨יד נִתְּנָה־ לּ֜וֹ מֵאֵ֧ת מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל דְּבַר־ י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמ֖וֹ עַד־ י֣וֹם מוֹת֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃
